Do I need root to use 80bee?
No. 80bee runs privileged commands through Shizuku on your own phone, or through ADB and Fastboot when another device is plugged in over USB OTG. Root is never required.
What\'s the difference between Local and OTG mode?
Local mode uses Shizuku to tweak the phone 80bee is installed on. OTG mode turns your phone into an ADB/Fastboot host so you can manage a second device connected with a USB OTG cable or adapter.
How do I set up Shizuku?

Install Shizuku from Google Play, F-Droid, or GitHub. Enable Wireless Debugging in Developer Options, start Shizuku from its app, then open 80bee and allow access when prompted. Shizuku needs to be started again after each reboot.
My OTG device isn\'t connecting. What should I check?

Enable USB Debugging on the target device (Settings > Developer Options), use a cable or adapter that supports data, and accept both the USB permission prompt on this phone and the \"Allow USB debugging\" prompt on the target.

Why are some tools greyed out?
Tools such as the Magisk Patcher and Bootloader Utilities talk to the bootloader over Fastboot, which is only available in OTG mode with the target device connected by USB.

Android 14+ introduces strict Calculated Sound Dose monitoring which aggressively dampens headphone and Bluetooth playback volumes once rolling safety limits are exceeded. Bypassing this stops the system warnings and automatic volume throttling.

Deletes the bypass keys and re-enables standard Android volume safety guidelines (recommended if sharing device with children).

Android devices feature distinct boot partitions for recovery, flashing, and system operation. Changing boot states requires ADB shell reboot privileges.
Warm reboot the device back into the standard Android system.
Boot into the recovery partition. Useful for clearing system cache, sideloading official OTA zips, or initiating factory resets.
Boot into low-level bootloader/boot ROM mode. Required to execute fastboot commands (e.g. flashing partitions, unlocking bootloader).
Boot into user-space Fastboot (available on Android 10+). Needed for flashing dynamic / logical partitions (system, product, vendor).

Unlocking the bootloader allows booting custom kernels, recovery partitions (TWRP), and custom ROMs (LineageOS). Warning: Unlocking/Relocking the bootloader triggers a hardware factory reset and wipes all user data on the device.
Triggers the hardware unlocking sequence. Requires physical confirmation on the device volume/power keys.
